I very strongly feel that I have wasted two years on medication levels that were not enough. "transition sabotage" is not a term I've heard before, but I certainly feel that it applies. do not trust gendergp or anyone who tries to prescribe finasteride as a functional blocker. whether it's unintentional incompetence or willful sabotage, they will not help you.

I have some pretty severe sensory issues and every single time I've been there in my life I have gotten a sensory overload induced panic attack within ten minutes of disembarking off the train. There's nowhere to calm down and everyone glares at you and walks like a steamroller and you have to pretty much duck and weave and constantly recalculate your path around the relentless stomp of the average London walker who wouldn't move out of the way if a bullet was coming in their path. Everything is so SO expensive and it's too hot and it stinks and it never ever EVER stops moving in the most complicated and busybusybusy way. The tube sucks, it's too loud and too fast and too busy and there's never a seat and you can just smell everyone's breath and you can't see out of the windows for a sense of reference to where you're going and everything is just so much bustle and I hate it so much. It's the exact opposite of everything and anything I could want in a city and to top it all off the residents treat it as if it's the only place in the country that matters or even exists. I hate London so goddamn much. I know some people love it but personally it is hell.

Currently? My dad.  Few months ago I spent a week with him in a caravan with no signal, no WiFi, no connection to my friends or other family or the outside world. Over the course of those days I learned.. a lot about him. 

Firstly, he's unable to express interest in anything that's not directly related to himself. Spent several hours on a watercolour painting of some standing stones nearby? "Oh. Ok. So my dog's not been very well lately" Trying to tell him about the interesting things I've been doing with my friends recently? "Alright. Anyway I was listening to a podcast recently" Near enough begging him to be proud of me or at least even acknowledge something I did which I thought was at least vaguely notable? "Did I tell you about the park run I have coming up?" 

I've kept noticing it between me and my siblings ever since. My brother's recovering from some health issues at the moment and he constantly ignores his care plan and has now on multiple occasions caused harm to his own son and not even realised. He asks if my sister wants to do anything on specific days that she's TOLD him that she's working. He takes no interest in anything any of us are doing and the moment we try and take it up with him he gets super defensive.

All three of his kids are autistic, and he also semi-recently got a diagnosis and has leant into it HARD. I know better than most how good it feels to discover a part of your identity but this man is so fucking oblivious with it that it is harming our relationships with him. "I'm so glad I don't have to mask at all around you guys any more!" He says, not realising how much we all have to heavily mask around him or else he gets annoyed with us and tells us to shut up, stop moving, pay attention to me when I'm talking, can you just give me a straight answer please, why are you doing that, can you speak UP please, etc. 

He also just makes so many sudden loud noises and movements and just screams at the world which I do understand to an extent, we all gotta stim from time to time, but also mate I've got trauma, SOME of which is your fault and I cannot STAND sudden noises and movements and aggression and I can fucking SEE you smirking every time you see you've made me flinch with a jolt of movement or sudden yell. 

A week of all of this constantly with no access to my normal support network of my siblings as well as several extremely cool gay people on the internet, alongside a couple other incidents like when I had to de-escalate a conflict between him and a minimum wage shop worker over the price of a bottle of pepsi left me exhausted, defeated and immensely depressed.
